entries.title: Robert Lewandowski scores again, but Fire settle for tie with Sounders
entries.summary: <p>SEATTLE — Dejan Joveljić scored a goal in each half of his debut with Seattle, but Maren Haile-Selassie and Robert Lewandowski answered for Chicago as the Sounders and Fire played to a 2-2 draw on Saturday.</p><p>Seattle grabbed the lead when Joveljić scored in the 12th minute, using assists from rookie Sebastian Gomez — his first — and defender Kalani Kossa-Rienzi — his second. It was the ninth goal of the season for Joveljić, who arrived this week after a $6 million cash-for-player trade with Sporting Kansas City.</p><p>Chicago pulled even in the 38th minute on Haile-Selassie's fifth goal, one off his career high. Lewandowski notched his fourth assist in his first seven league matches, and defender Andrew Gutman collected his fifth of the campaign.</p><p>Joveljić scored again to give the Sounders a 2-1 lead three minutes into the second half. Albert Rusnák picked up his eighth assist and 19-year-old Snyder Brunell his second.</p><p>Lewandowski used his head to score his fifth goal for the equalizer in the 82nd minute. Haile-Selassie earned his eighth assist to match his career high set in each of the last two seasons. Rookie Puso Dithejane snagged his first assist.</p><p>Chris Brady stopped one shot for Chicago (11-6-4). Brady topped 10,000 career minutes in the 34th on Saturday. He is Chicago’s second homegrown player to reach the mark.</p><p>Andrew Thomas totaled nine saves for Seattle (7-9-5), which is 6-0-3 all time at home against the Fire.</p><p>Joveljić is the fifth player to score in his debut with the Sounders and the second to score twice, joining Fredy Montero (2009), Nelson Valdez (2015), Pedro de la Vega (2024) and Brunell (2025). Montero scored two goals in Seattle's 3-0 win over the New York Red Bulls in the first match of the Sounders' debut season.</p><p>Chicago went 3-0-2 in August and improved to 4-3-4 on the road in its climb to third place in the Eastern Conference.</p><p><b>Up next</b></p><p>Chicago: At Toronto FC on Saturday.</p><p>Seattle: Hosts New York Red Bulls on Saturday.</p>

entries.title: Motorcyclist dies after colliding with SUV in Archer Heights
entries.summary: <p>A 34-year-old motorcyclist died Saturday after he was struck by an SUV in Archer Heights, Chicago police said.</p><p>The crash happened at 1:48 p.m. in the 4800 block of South Archer Avenue, according to police.</p><p>A 35-year-old woman was traveling southbound in an Audi SUV on Hamlin Avenue when she allegedly failed to yield the right of way and struck the man who had been riding a motorcycle west on Archer Avenue, police said.</p><p>The man was taken to Mount Sinai Hospital, where police said he was later pronounced dead.</p><p>The woman was taken to St. Anthony’s Hospital and was initially issued at least one citation, police said.</p><p>The Major Accident Investigation Unit is investigating.</p>

entries.title: Bears-Titans training-camp report: Luther Burden looks '100%'
entries.summary: <p>NASHVILLE, Tenn. — Breaking down the Bears’ 24-15 preseason win against the Titans on Saturday night at Nissan Stadium: </p><h3><b>What happened</b></h3><p>With most the Bears’ starters sitting, quarterback Tyson Bagent threw a 97-yard touchdown pass to rookie Zavion Thomas on their first offensive play and never trailed the rest of the way. Bagent finished with a 156.9 passer rating. Roschon Johnson led all rushers with 12 carries for 41 yards. The Bears defense didn’t give up a touchdown until there was less than four minutes remaining.</p><h3><b>Burden good</b></h3><p>Hours before kickoff, Caleb Williams threw to the Bears' regular starters — among them, Luther Burden, who is recovering from a groin injury. Coach Ben Johnson said "he looks 100% to me," a good sign given that the season opener is two weeks away. </p><h3><b>J.T, on the call</b></h3><p>Quarterbacks coach J.T. Barrett called plays in the second half. Receivers coach Antwaan Randle-El handled the second half of Game 1 and tight ends coach Jim Dray called plays in the second half of Game 2.</p><h3><b>A stadium!</b></h3><p>The Titans are building the new Nissan Stadium just feet from the original, set to open next year, and have already been granted the Super Bowl at the end of the 2029 season. The Titans got a sweetheart deal from local authorities the Bears could only dream of — when the Nashville sports authority pledged $760 million the state $500 million more in 2022, it marked the most public funding ever for an NFL stadium.</p><p><b>What’s next</b><br>The Bears must trim their rosters from 90 players to 53 by 5 p.m. Sunday.</p>

entries.title: Man found in critical condition after Chicago Lawn shooting
entries.summary: <p>A 53-year-old man was in critical condition Saturday after he suffered multiple gunshot wounds in Chicago Lawn, Chicago police said.</p><p>Officers responded to the 2600 block of West 63rd Street at 2:20 p.m. and found the man with a gunshot wound in the chest and arm, police said.</p><p>He was taken to the University of Chicago Medical Center and is currently in critical condition, according to police.</p><p>Area 1 detectives are investigating.</p>

entries.title: Still rebuilding, Gary celebrates city on Michael Jackson’s birthday
entries.summary: <p>A French couple from Martinique, a Russian artist from California, and an 8-year-old Arkansas boy traveling with his grandmother made a pilgrimage to Gary.</p><p>The sacred day was Michael Jackson’s birthday, and the place of devotion on Saturday was his modest childhood home at 2300 Jackson Street. They mingled with other disciples who delivered bouquets, tied locks to the fence and scribbled messages on the sidewalk. </p><p>Some wore fedoras, bedazzled gloves and replicas of his signature jackets. Most sang along as his hits blasted from the speakers, and a few brave souls busted a move, including one person who danced on top of a van.</p><p>Residents also joined to pay their respects to their hometown hero as the city hosted a “Greater Gary” festival outside nearby Roosevelt High School.</p><p>“It makes us feel good that everyone is coming from across the world to MJ’s house,” said Debbie entries.title: Darrell Mattison's big defensive play helps Morgan Park beat Notre Dame
entries.summary: <p>Being the best athlete on the field comes with greater expectations.</p><p>So it is with Morgan Park senior safety Darrell Mattison, who made the biggest defensive play in the Mustangs’ 26-10 win Saturday afternoon against Notre Dame at Hanson Stadium.</p><p>Midway through the fourth quarter, Notre Dame running back Christopher Love raced around the right side toward the end zone. Mattison chased him down from behind for a touchdown-saving tackle, and the Dons wound up turning the ball over on downs.</p><p>Had Love scored and the Dons made the two-point conversion, the game would’ve been tied at 18. But Morgan Park (1-1) stayed ahead and sealed it when Ronald Smith Jr. and Dacari Blandin teamed up for their second touchdown with 1:21 left.</p><p>Mattison is a four-star prospect who decommitted from one of the best programs in the country (Michigan) this summer to commit to another one (Ole Miss).</p><p>Mustangs coach Chris James saw Mattison’s tackle of Love as routine — for him.</p><p>“It’s something he’s supposed to do,” James said. “Like, if you’re a D1 athlete, you’re supposed to give maximum effort. . . . If you’re a four-star guy, then you make that play. And he made that play.</p><p>“But he’s got to play better, and I want him to know that. He leaves too many plays on the field where those are plays that a guy with that ability should make. . . . And he won’t mind me saying that.”</p><p>Mattison had five tackles, broke up several passes and drew a pass-interference call on one of his offensive snaps.</p><p>“He’s got to make a few more [when] he’s got his hands on the ball, like that one-handed pick. I expect him to make that play. . . . So I expect him to play way better in Week 3.”</p><p>Mattison is comfortable with straight talk from coaches. It’s one of the things that attracted him to Ole Miss, where Pete Golding was promoted from defensive coordinator last November when Lane Kiffin left for LSU.</p><div class="RelatedList Enhancement" data-module data-align-center> <div class="RelatedList-title">Related</div> <ul class="RelatedList-items"> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/high-school-football/2026/08/29/st-rita-football-chicago-glenbard-west" >St. Rita beats Glenbard West on a two-point conversion in the final minute</a> </li> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/high-school-football/2026/08/28/high-school-football-super-25-scores-sun-times-chicago" >How the Super 25 fared in Week 2</a> </li> </ul> </div> <p>“He’s just a great guy,” Mattison said. “He’s a real funny guy, really up-front and blunt. He’s gonna keep it so real with you.”</p><p>Mattison isn’t looking ahead, though. After losing to ranked Downers Grove North by five and beating Notre Dame, he said his goal — like James’ — is to keep improving.</p><p>“It’s just small details,” Mattison said. “Just doing the things we’ve got to do, the small things like getting set, getting ready, make the plays.”</p><p>Morgan Park’s offense made its share of plays. Smith Jr., back as the Mustangs’ quarterback, was 15-for-20 for 182 yards and three touchdowns with one interception. Blandin had six catches for 63 yards and two touchdowns, and Will Smith Jr. had 19 carries for 152 yards, including a 40-yard touchdown.</p><p>“[Ronald Smith Jr.] is a guy that, with time, he just gets better,” James said. “He made the plays he needed to make, but he has got to be more consistent, too.”</p><p>For Notre Dame (1-1), quarterback Eric Couper completed 13 of 29 passes for 122 yards, including a 20-yard touchdown to Jon Miro. Love had 21 carries for 80 yards.</p><p>“Morgan Park’s everything we thought they were: speed athletes all over the field, big kids, well-coached, execute very well,” Dons coach Dan DeFranza said. “I also think that we proved that we’re a pretty good team ourselves. . . . The fact that we faced a team like Morgan Park before we get to the Catholic League, to see that speed and physicality is good.”</p>

entries.title: West Town drive-by shooting leaves 1 critically injured
entries.summary: <p>A person was critically injured in a shooting Saturday evening in West Town, Chicago police said. </p><p>Officers responded to a call of a person shot along the 1500 block of West Augusta Boulevard at 8:33 p.m., according to police.</p><p>The victim, described as a male whose age was not disclosed, was reportedly outside when a dark-colored SUV drove by, and an unknown person opened fire, police said.</p><p>The victim suffered two gunshot wounds to the chest and was treated at the scene by Chicago Fire Department personnel.</p><p>He was later taken to Stroger Hospital, where he was listed in critical condition.</p><p>No further details were available, including the victim’s age, according to police.</p><p>Area 4 detectives are investigating the shooting, police said. </p>

entries.title: 1 critically wounded in Humboldt Park shooting
entries.summary: <p>A 29-year-old man was critically injured in a shooting Saturday evening in Humboldt Park, according to Chicago police.</p><p>The man had been near a sidewalk along the 700 block of North Ridgeway Avenue when he was struck in the buttocks at 7:55 p.m., police said.</p><p>The victim was taken to Mount Sinai Hospital and was reported in critical condition, according to police.</p><p>Detectives are investigating. No suspects are in custody.</p>

entries.title: Blackhawks' Frank Nazar hopes to convert opportunities this season with new teeth, new teammate
entries.summary: <p><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks" target="_blank" >Blackhawks</a> forward Frank Nazar is tired of his dentist.</p><p>‘‘Thank you, but, man, hopefully I don’t have to see you again,’’ Nazar told him this summer.</p><p>It’s nothing personal. It’s just that the easygoing 22-year-old endured enough discomfort and chewing difficulty after suffering a broken jaw in December. When two of his front teeth got knocked out during the Hawks’ third-to-last game in April, it felt a little bit like a curse.</p><p>With the teeth replaced, he no longer speaks with a lisp, but rather with ‘‘just a little bit of a whistle every now and then.’’ Nazar isn’t banking on this particular pair of fake teeth sticking around for life, though.</p><p>‘‘Hopefully I can go at least a year without seeing [my dentist] again for those reasons, [not for] a cleaning or something,’’ he joked. ‘‘But that’s hockey, and that’s how it goes. It’s what you sign up for. No complaints.’’</p><p>Nazar has split his time this offseason between Chicago and his hometown of Detroit. He thinks it’s important to enjoy some relaxation time with family and old friends back home so that Chicago ‘‘feels like something new’’ whenever he returns.</p><p>But he also has fallen in love with Chicago summers, aside from the fact that Lake Michigan water is ‘‘a little cold.’’ Training-wise, he mostly has worked in-person with Hawks skills coach Brian Keane.</p><p>They haven’t done anything revolutionary, but sometimes that’s for the best. Nazar is coming off a solid first full NHL season (15 goals and 26 assists in 66 games), but he needs to keep developing in all areas.</p><p>‘‘I’ve focused a lot on using my speed to attack wide or drive the play,’’ Nazar said. ‘‘And then if plays aren’t there, pulling and finding something late or finding the slot. [I’m] always trying to threaten with my feet and legs and speed.</p><p>‘‘Honestly, it’s all pretty similar [to previous years]. It’s just getting better at those things. . . . [Lightning forward Nikita Kucherov] does a thousand rims a day, all summer long. But he’s not bad at rims. He’s not changing up his play style. He’s just perfecting.’’</p><p>One change from Nazar’s previous summers has been a stronger emphasis on conditioning because he has learned how grueling the NHL can be. He has spent abundant time on exercise bikes.</p><p>‘‘Honestly, it’s getting to the point where I don’t even want to look at a bike,’’ he quipped.</p><p>Last season, he raced out with 11 points in 11 games in October before falling dramatically off that pace. He had only 13 points — including only two goals — in his next 32 games before picking things up again in March. Better conditioning might give him a better chance of avoiding a winter drought.</p><p>‘‘I’m focused on going into training camp . . . making sure everyone knows I worked hard this summer, I’m ready to go for the season and I want to win,’’ he said.</p><p>‘‘Another big thing I focused on this summer was bearing down on opportunities. Even if we’re up one or two goals, [I want to be] ready to score, end the game and take the will away from other teams.’’</p><p>On that note, the Hawks’ late-game struggles last season have lingered in his mind, motivating him to grind through the toughest days.</p><p>The Hawks allowed nine game-tying or -deciding goals in the final four minutes of third periods last season, letting a number of near victories slip away. Then they went 4-9 in overtimes and 3-5 in shootouts, losing out on more potential points.</p><p>‘‘I know there were chances in some of those games that I had where, if I score, the game is over and we win,’’ Nazar said. ‘‘I think about those every day on the ice and in the gym. . . . You’ve got to go into each day as a new day, so it’s not something that’s holding me back. But if I get a chance like that, I don’t want to make the same mistake.’’</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" > <div class="TweetUrl"> <blockquote class="twitter-tweet"><p lang="en" dir="ltr">Blackhawks forward Frank Nazar receives many texts about Denver injury attorney Frank Azar's notorious billboards, naturally.<br><br>But this one really made him laugh: "I couldn't believe it. I thought my eyes were deceiving me... I didn't tell him to do that!" <a href="https://t.co/kpRhkQs1EV">https://t.co/kpRhkQs1EV</a></p>— Ben Pope (@BenPopeCST) <a href="https://x.com/BenPopeCST/status/2092755978445881476?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">August 26, 2026</a></blockquote> <script async src="https://platform.x.com/widgets.js" charset="utf-8"></script> </div> </div> </div></div><p></p><h3><b>Observing Kane</b></h3><p>Nazar, <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks/2026/08/23/blackhawks-alex-vlasic-playoffs-louis-crevier-bowen-byram-patrick-kane" target="_blank" >like defenseman Alex Vlasic</a>, feels confident the ultra-young Hawks will take a step forward in 2026-27. He wants to ‘‘show the league that age doesn’t matter.’’</p><p>And, like Vlasic, Nazar also has spent a lot of time skating this summer with franchise legend/newcomer Patrick Kane.</p><p>‘‘You would hear the rumors that he’s choosing between a few different teams,’’ Nazar said. “Every time on the ice, I would joke with our skills coaches, ‘I’m going extra hard today so [Kane] will sign here.’ And then we walk in one morning, and there’s a thousand cameras there. We’re all looking at each other like, ‘[Kane] must have signed.’ It was a great day.’’</p><p>Kane later mentioned during his news conference that he has been impressed by Nazar’s work ethic and speed, prompting Nazar to wonder whether they’ll end up playing together. Especially while Connor Bedard recovers from shoulder surgery, that might be the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks/2026/07/26/projecting-blackhawks-lines-patrick-kane-bowen-byram-connor-bedard-frank-nazar" target="_blank" >most likely scenario</a>.</p><p>Nazar, of course, has watched Kane equally closely, if not more so. Among his observations has been one of the subtle keys to Kane’s incredible ability to possess the puck: The majority of his stick movements are purely deceptive.</p><p>‘‘He’s really good at pushing the puck into spaces,’’ Nazar said. ‘‘It’s funny. Everyone is, like, ‘Oh, his hands are great.’ And they are great, obviously. But the puck is not always on his stick when he’s stick-handling. If someone’s trying to slash him, the puck is not always on his stick to push away.’’</p><p>Nazar then proclaimed that he’s ready to ‘‘run through a wall’’ for Kane this season.</p><p>It remains to be seen exactly how much closer the 37-year-old future Hall of Famer will push the Hawks to playoff contention — and exactly how he’ll fit into a locker room populated by a younger generation. But there’s certainly no lack of anticipation.</p><p>The wait to find out is getting shorter, too. Training camp is expected to start Sept. 16 or 17, giving the Hawks just a few days to prepare for their preseason opener Sept. 19 and less than two weeks to prepare for their regular-season opener Sept. 29.</p><h3><b>Korchinski signed</b></h3><p>The Hawks signed defenseman Kevin Korchinski to a new two-year contract carrying a $1.325 million salary-cap hit Saturday, leaving defenseman Ethan Del Mastro as their only remaining restricted free agent. </p><p>Korchinski is no longer waivers-exempt, so he will be on the NHL roster this season. But the former seventh overall pick enters training camp without an abundantly clear route to consistent playing time. He has two years to change his so-far disappointing career trajectory.</p>

entries.title: Famous Packers fan Lil Wayne takes aim at Bears, tells Ben Johnson to ‘put his shirt back on’
entries.summary: <p>Five-time Grammy winner Lil Wayne released a Packers anthem this week called “Special Ops” with disses fired at the other three NFC North teams. When he got to <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >the Bears</a>, he went right at their leader with a direct shot at coach <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2025/09/01/the-bears-and-their-fans-needed-a-truth-teller-they-got-one-in-new-coach-ben-johnson" >Ben Johnson</a>.</p><p>The song was released in conjunction with the team revealing its new Nike rivalry jerseys, which they will wear for their Week 5 home game against the Bears in October.</p><p>About halfway through it, he said, “If the coach in Chicago want to act up, we want all of the smoke, no tobacco.” Shortly after he went for Johnson again with, “Tell your coach put his shirt back on, I got Bear fur on my floor at home, We gon’ make you eat all them words, And may they taste like Provolone.”</p><p>It then pivoted to stanza about how the Bears “still suck,” the Vikings are “still drunk” and the Lions’ “tails tucked.”</p><p>Lil Wayne grew up in New Orleans, but became a Packers fan as a kid when they won the Super Bowl over the Patriots there in 1997.</p><p>“I love them,” he explained in a 2023 appearance on NBC. “They won the Super Bowl in New Orleans. I was hooked. My dad went to the Super Bowl and came back home with memorabilia, and it was all ‘Green Bay champs.’ So every day I’m using a ‘Green Bay champs’ cup, I’m showering with a Green Bay towel. I’m a Green Bay fan.”</p><p>He ran out of the tunnel with the team before a game at Lambeau Field that season as well, saying he and coach Matt LaFleur are “real, real, real good friends.” The Packers also have embraced Lil Wayne over the years and posted about him on their website and social media channels.</p>

entries.title: Dear Abby: Daughter's Unemployed Fiance Fails To Impress Mom
entries.summary: <p><b>DEAR ABBY:</b> One year ago, I convinced my daughter (64) to move here to Florida to be closer to me. I bought her a small mobile home to live in, and I don't charge her any rent. Before she moved down here from Minnesota, she agreed to pay the lot rent and her own utilities.</p><p>Recently, she met a man and fell in love. She has been single and self-supporting for more than 20 years, but she says she's lonely and wants someone to talk to when she gets home from work. She thinks this man fits the bill. He is 60 and doesn't have a job, a car or a place to live. He has been staying with a friend for the entire two months she has known him. He has given her an engagement ring after two months, and they plan on marrying later this year.</p><p>My daughter asked me if I'm happy for her. When I told her if she is lonesome when she comes home from work, she should consider getting a pet, she laughed. I do not think two months is long enough. In my opinion, her fiance should at least have a job — and a car would be nice so she wouldn't have to take the bus to work every day. What should I tell her if she asks me if she should marry him? — <i>CONCERNED MOM</i></p><p><b>DEAR CONCERNED MOM:</b> She won't ask, because she knows she won't like the answer. However, if she does, give your honest opinion — and tell her that I share it. A legal union with this man who has nothing would be foolish and self-destructive. Instead of planning a wedding, his time and energy would be better spent looking for work.</p><p><b>DEAR ABBY:</b> I am receiving physical therapy at a center with a huge TV on the wall. It is on the entire time, playing stuff like sports and home improvement shows. I find it tedious, stressful and distracting.</p><p>Importantly, due to my declining hearing, the TV makes it difficult to understand the young physical therapist I'm working with. I have told her several times now that because of the background noise, I need her to face me, not the TV, so I can hear her. She tends to forget this fact. I have even asked about playing music instead of the TV, to no avail.</p><p>I would go somewhere else, but this is the only place my insurance pays for. I dread going there because of this. Am I wrong to want a quiet environment in which to heal? — <i>PEACEFUL IN FLORIDA</i></p><p><b>DEAR PEACEFUL:</b> You are not wrong. Your physical therapist appears to have a listening problem. Rather than continue to complain to this employee, talk to the manager of the therapy center and explain the problem.</p><p><b>DEAR ABBY:</b> This may seem like a silly question, but when filling out paperwork that asks if I am married, divorced or widowed, I'm not sure what to put down. I was divorced, but then he died. Does it matter which answer I choose? — <i>BEFUDDLED IN INDIANA</i></p><p><b>DEAR BEFUDDLED:</b> This is not a silly question. It is one I have been asked before. The correct answer is that you are divorced. If your ex-husband remarried after your divorce, the woman he married is his widow.</p>

entries.title: Black & Bronze festival returns to the South Side
entries.summary: <p>Looking for water, South Side native Denise Moore waved down a young boy carrying a handful of bottles. She asked where she could find some, and he gave her detailed directions to the food truck selling them.</p><p>“That's what it's all about,” Moore said. “He's already understanding to be helpful. Maybe because he saw the gray in my hair and thought, OK, this is an elder. But that's the respect.”</p><p>For organizers of Chicago's Black & Bronze Festival, that kind of interaction was the point.</p><p>They wanted the annual Bronzeville festival to recreate the feeling of the traditional front porch — a place where generations naturally crossed paths, where children learned from elders, neighbors looked out for one another and stories moved from one generation to the next.</p><p>“Where grandma and the grandbabies and aunts and uncles and cousins were all together,” founder Jessica La Rel said.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div entries.title: 1 man killed, 2 people injured after shooter fired shots into a crowd gathered in Douglas
entries.summary: <p>One man died and two others were injured when a shooter fired several shots into a crowd late Saturday in the Douglas neighborhood, Chicago police said.</p><p>The crowd was gathered in the 100 block of East 37th Street when the shooting started around 11:20 p.m., according to police.</p><p>Three people were hit and taken to University of Chicago Medical Center, police said. A 32-year-old man, shot several times, was in critical condition but later pronounced dead. A 31-year-old man was also in critical condition. A 23-year-old woman, shot in her hand, was in good condition.</p>

entries.title: 1 person died, 9 injured in Washington Park mass shooting
entries.summary: <p>One person died and nine others were injured in a mass shooting late Saturday in Washington Park, Chicago police said.</p><p>Officers were trying to disperse a large crowd of people that had gathered on the eastern edge of the park in the 5400 block of South Cottage Grove Avenue when the mass shooting happened about 11:30 p.m. Saturday, according to police.</p><p>A 35-year-old man shot multiple times was taken to University of Chicago Medical Center where he was pronounced dead. </p><p>Six other victims — men and women ages 26 to 45 — were all in good condition at the University of Chicago, Stroger Hospital and St. Bernard Hospital, police said in a statement. Authorities did not know the condition of the three remaining victims — ages 23, 35 and 37 — nor the hospital they were taken to.</p><p>No officers were injured. Police did not report how many shooters fired at the crowd, and no one has been arrested.</p>

entries.title: Bears trade DT Gervon Dexter to Falcons for CB Clark Phillips III, draft pick
entries.summary: <p>The <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a> started cut day with a trade, agreeing to send defensive tackle Gervon Dexter to the Falcons for cornerback Clark Phillips III and a 2027 fifth-round pick Sunday morning, a source confirmed.</p><p>The <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/halas-intrigue/2026/08/29/bears-titans-podcast-halas-intrigue" target="_blank" >Bears</a> added depth to a defensive backs room that desperately needed it. Phillips, 24, has started seven games and appeared in 21 more in three seasons with the Falcons. A triceps injury in Week 4 last season cost him the rest of the year. He's due to be a free agent at the end of this season.</p><p>Former Bears assistant general manager Ian Cunningham, who was named the Falcons GM this winter — and is one of Bears GM Ryan Poles' best friends — knows what he's getting in Dexter. He was on the Bears staff that made him a second-round pick in 2023. Dexter, 24, was entering the final year of his rookie deal and wanted a contract extension, which made him a popular trade candidate dating back to the spring. </p><p>The Bears wanted him to play with lower pad level. Dexter left practice Tuesday with what the team claimed was a hamstring injury and did not travel with the Bears to Nashville for the joint practice and exhibition finale.</p><p>Dexter had lost his starting job during training camp practices in the past week. The Bears have used Kentavius Street, Neville Gallimore and rookie Jordan van den Berg next to Grady Jarrett. One of the two veterans figures to start Week 1. The Bears have been intrigued by van den Berg's motor and athleticism during training camp, too.</p><p>Still, trading Dexter is risky. Dexter started all 19 games last year — 17 games plus two playoff appearances — and has played in 49 of a possible 51 regular-season games during his three-year career. He finished second on the team with six sacks last year and totaled 13 1/2 in three seasons.</p><p>Even with Dexter on board, the Bears' defensive line was one of the team's perceived weaknesses entering the season. They finished second-to-last in the NFL in pass-rush win rate last year and were among one of the worst defenses against the run. The team is trading from a weakness, not a strength. </p><p>"We've challenged [Dexter] to do some technique things a little bit different this year," coach Ben Johnson said this week. "When he does it, it's a beautiful thing, because he is a strong, he is a big man and he's willing to run guys down sideline to sideline. I think that's what's awesome. The consistency level is what we're still trying to get on a day-in, day-out, play-in, play-out perspective. But when he does it right, does it the way that we're looking for, it's a pretty thing."</p><p>The Falcons made Phillips a fourth-round pick out of Utah in 2023. He started playing for the Utes the year after Bears cornerback Jaylon Johnson was drafted out of the school.</p><p>Johnson seemed to hurt his right arm during Thursday's joint practice, while fellow cornerback Tyrique Stevenson was in an out of practice after hurting his leg. Neither injury is considered overly serious. Slot cornerback Kyler Gordon's mysterious calf injury has loomed over the Bears' entire preseason — he's yet to practice and team officials are a combination of frustrated and bewildered by his slow recovery. Johnson has taken to giving curt one-word answers when asked about his status. Jaylon Jones hurt his hamstring against the Titans on Saturday night.</p><p>Cam Lewis, who was put in the slot at the start of camp, was moved to safety after the team lost big-money free-agent Coby Bryant to a serious knee injury. He's expected to miss most of the season.</p><p>The 5-foot-9, 183-pound Phillips played mostly outside cornerback in 2023 and 2024. Pro Football Focus gave him their 20th-best coverage grade among all cornerbacks in 2024 — tied with Gordon. </p><p>The fifth-round pick the Bears acquired helps to make up for the loss of their own 2027 fifth-rounder, which they sent to the Patriots for center Garrett Bradbury in March.</p><p>The Bears played their final preseason game Saturday night. Like the rest of the NFL, they have to make final cuts to their roster by 5 p.m. Sunday.</p>

entries.title: Bulls' Noa Essengue earning short leash as a puppy that won't bite
entries.summary: <p>Pro Football Hall of Fame coach Bill Parcells wasn’t one to sugarcoat.</p><p>In talking about passive-minded rookies, Parcells once said, “If they don’t bite when they’re puppies, they usually won’t bite.”</p><p>It’s a different sport, but the adage applies when it comes to the Bulls’ Noa Essengue. That puppy ain’t biting. Heck, he’s not even nipping.</p><p>There’s even worse news for the second-year French forward.</p><p>According to a source, he has been spoken to about his lack of physicality and been warned about his emotions on the court. More important, the new regime didn’t draft him, so while it’s in the business of development, it’s not going to follow a path of blind loyalty.</p><p>No, that was strictly for the Arturas Karnisovas regime.</p><p>As Summer League showed, Essengue will be treated with tough love and will be on a short leash. If that message doesn’t sink in quickly, don’t be surprised if the No. 12 overall pick from the 2025 draft is shopped in a package at some point this season.</p><p>No organization is looking to give up on a 19-year-old, 6-11 prospect, but new executive vice president of basketball operations Bryson Graham also knows that it doesn’t take long for prospect to become suspect.</p><p>Graham is from the school of SLAP (size, length, athleticism, physicality). Essengue’s school is SLIM (soft, long, intimidated, mild). SLIM is going to become none — as in playing time — quickly.</p><p>New coach Tiago Splitter demonstrated that last month in Las Vegas, starting Essengue in the first game and quickly making him a bench player by the second half and for the remaining games.</p><p>Splitter even had a chance to throw a life preserver Essengue’s way when asked if the tentativeness could’ve been a result of the shoulder surgery that cost Essengue most of his rookie season, and Splitter opted to keep him treading water.</p><p>“I don’t know if it’s because of the injury,” Splitter said. “He’s got to maybe bring a little more force in everything he does. That’s something we’re working on.”</p><p>That’s all well and good, but what if Parcells is spot on. If Essengue doesn’t have bite in his game at 19, does it magically appear at 20 or 21?</p><p>“That’s something he’s got to do,” Splitter said. “Yeah, we’re going to keep pushing him.”</p><p>Next month’s training camp will be vital for Essengue. The Bulls aren’t looking for him to become some sort of enforcer, but being knocked down every other time up the floor and looking like a baby giraffe instead of a talented lottery pick was not in the plans.</p><p>This is now on Essengue to fix.</p><p>And it’s also another reminder of the stain left behind from the Karnisovas era.</p><p>The old front office suffered from poor talent evaluation.</p><p>Karnisovas settled on Patrick Williams with the No. 4 pick in 2020, while multiple scouts and most of the draft room wanted Tyrese Haliburton.</p><p>Karnisovas not only was fixated on Williams, but he didn’t even consider Haliburton a serious prospect. A source indicated that Karnisovas didn’t even think Haliburton would be a top-four talent on the Bulls’ roster at the time.</p><p>Before his Achilles injury in the 2025 NBA Finals, there was an argument to be made that Haliburton was a top-four talent in the entire Eastern Conference.</p><p>A source that used to be in the organization said Bulls scouts liked Joan Beringer — another French player — more than Essengue, but because voices that opposed Karnisovas often fell on deaf ears or were pushed out of the organization, there was little resistance offered up.</p><p>An NBA source told the Sun-Times this week that one organization didn’t even have Essengue in the top 20 of that draft.</p><p>The reason was his lack of physicality.</p><p>The puppy didn’t bite.</p>

entries.summary: <p>Mount Carmel’s thrilling comeback win on ESPN turned a lot of heads Friday night, but the Caravan beating a team from New Jersey doesn’t make waves in the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/super-25-football-rankings/2026/08/23/high-school-football-rankings-chicago-illinois-sun-times-michael-obrien" >Super 25</a>.</p><p>When it comes to local rankings and Illinois high school football reputation makers, the biggest moment of the season so far was Sandburg’s 35-28 win against Montini in Orland Park.</p><p>The Broncos had won <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/high-school-football/2026/08/15/montini-football-israel-abrams-ihsa" >25 consecutive games</a> and two state championships since their last loss. Miami recruit Israel Abrams is the No. 3 quarterback in the country according to 247Sports.com. And Montini is much more than just one great player. Mike Bukovsky, one of the state’s most experienced coaches, has college talent all over his roster.</p><p>Abrams played well in the defeat, finishing with 233 passing yards, but a few key turnovers did the Broncos in.</p><p>Sandburg doesn’t have a national or even a local star player. And the Eagles’ coach, Sheamus Murphy, is in just his second season at the helm. Murphy coached Back of the Yards from 2015-2018 before joining Sandburg as an assistant.</p><p>Sandburg quarterback Sean Ruisz missed the season opener with an injury but shook off the rust quickly. He was 14 of 17 passing for 226 yards with a touchdown and had 14 carries for 181 yards and three touchdowns.</p><p>Ruisz connected with NIU recruit Lucas Matykiewicz eight times for 88 yards and a TD. Army recruit Quinn Durkin contributed 84 receiving yards and 43 rushing yards for the Eagles.</p><p>Sandburg upset Lincoln-Way East late last season, but the Griffins played without star quarterback Jonas Williams. But the Bulldogs’ Week 2 road trip to Rochester did not go well.</p><p>The Rockets, a Class 4A powerhouse, knocked off Batavia 44-16. Vander Luitgaren threw for 237 yards but had three interceptions.</p><p>Rochester led 27-0 in the first quarter. The Bulldogs face undefeated Glenbard North on Friday.</p><h3>Steel success</h3><p>Joliet Central has won just two games over the past six seasons and only three over the last seven. entries.title: Bears transaction tracker — analyzing cut-day decisions
entries.summary: <p>The <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a> — and other NFL teams — need to cut their roster down from 90 players to 53 by 5 p.m. Sunday.</p><p>Teams can then begin assembling a 16-man practice squad Monday.</p><p>Tracking the moves the Bears are making Sunday:</p><h3>12:15 p.m.</h3><p>The Bears are cutting receiver J.P. Richardson, a source said.</p><h3>11:30 a.m.</h3><p>The Bears are cutting receiver <b>Scotty Miller</b>, a Barrington High School alum and former Super Bowl champion, per ESPN. </p><h3><b>7:45 a.m.</b></h3><p>The Bears <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/08/30/bears-trade-falcons-gervon-dexter-clark-phillips-cornerback-cut-day-trade-draft-pick-atlanta" target="_blank" >agreed to trade defensive tackle Gervon Dexter</a> to the Falcons in exchange for cornerback Clark Phillips III and a 2027 fifth-round pick.</p><p>Like Phillips, Dexter is entering the final year of his rookie contract. The Bears weren't willing to give him a contract extension and watched him fall behind in training camp. Veterans Kentavius Street and Neville Gallimore and rookie Jordan van den Berg had emerged as part of the team's interior rotation alongside Grady Jarrett.</p><p>Phillips, who missed most of last season with a triceps injury, plays outside cornerback. He's appeared in 28 games, starting seven times, since being drafted out of Utah.</p><h3><b>11 a.m.</b></h3><p>The Bears have released veteran wide receiver Scotty Miller, who spent the offseason with them, a source said. As a vested veteran, he immediately becomes a free agent and can sign elsewhere.</p><p>Miller, from Barrington, has played seven NFL seasons and had nine catches for 62 yards with the Steelers last season.</p><h3><b>12:45 p.m.</b></h3><p>The Bears released offensive lineman Jedrick Wills, a former first-round pick who hasn't played since 2024, a source said. </p>

entries.title: Security guard fatally shot at Gary train station by 9 law enforcement officers
entries.summary: <p>An armed security guard acting "unusual and erratic" near a Gary train station was fatally shot Friday night by six Gary police officers and three Lake County sheriff's deputies, authorities said.</p><p>Officers were called to Broadway and 4th Avenue by Gary's City Hall around 11 p.m. and confronted the security guard, Kenneth Williams, according to the Indiana State Police and Lake County coroner's office. Gary officers and Lake County deputies attempted to de-escalate the situation, but a "confrontation" with Williams led to a shootout, according to authorities. </p><p>Williams, 67, was pronounced dead at the scene. Six Gary police officers and three Lake County Sheriff’s officers fired their guns during the incident, Indiana State Police said in a statement.</p><p>The state police are investigating the incident. The officers involved are on administrative leave.</p>

entries.summary: <p>Women are human, right?</p><p>I'm fairly certain they are. They've got all the telltale signs. Complex thought processes. Self-motivation — and by that, I mean they can move, physically, although the other meaning, doing things of their own volition, is also a factor.</p><p>Now that I'm trying to define what being human means, I'm sorry for starting this way. It is fraught.</p><p>Next I almost suggested "bilateral symmetry" — meaning if you draw a line down the middle, we're the same on both sides — then thoughtlessly elaborated with "two arms, two legs" but realized, in the nick of time, I'd end up getting chewed out by amputees who are, of course, still human despise their losses. A big tent, people.</p><div class="RichTextSidebarModule Enhancement" data-module data-align-center><a class="AnchorLink" id="module-590000" name="module-590000"></a> <div class="RichTextSidebarModule-title">Opinion bug</div> <div class="RichTextModule-items RichTextBody"><h2>Opinion</h2></div> </div><p>Honestly, I feel like tossing the question to AI, after having looked askance at it last week. Contradictory, we humans ... oh heck, why not? Everybody else does. Hey AI. what does being human mean?</p><p>"Being human means living as a blend of biological existence, conscious self-awareness and emotional connection to the world and others."</p><p>Sounds right to me. And I did I hit the first two, physical and consciousness, on my own. As far as emotional connection... well, I'm not so sure about that. Could be more AI fantasy. Emotional <i>disconnection</i> seems all the rage nowadays — in fact, tossing people over the side of the humanity boat might be a defining mark of humanity. Everybody's doing it.</p><p>Immigration papers not in order? You can be guiltlessly shipped to some hellhole in Texas or Uganda.</p><p>On the other side of the Israeli-Palestinian struggle? Why you and everyone like you can just... magically vanish. In fact, that's the plan.</p><p>Gone through the difficult and daring process of living as a gender other than the one you were born with? You can't serve in the military and your driver's license is suddenly void in Kansas.</p><p>And don't start on women in 13 states who want to wrest control of their gynecological processes from the Lord God Almighty, where they belong, apparently.</p><p>“I felt dehumanized," Abbey Hall told the <a class="Link" href="https://indianacapitalchronicle.com/2024/10/21/in-her-words-traveling-to-illinois-for-abortion-care/" target="_blank" >Indiana Capital Chronicle</a> in 2024, of what happened after she discovered the baby she was carrying had a potentially fatal birth defect. "I felt like a criminal.”</p><p>And the mother of two would have been a criminal, too, in Indiana, had she tried to have an abortion, since her choice in the matter had been plucked out of her hands by men in Indianapolis, who are more moral and know better, in their own estimation.</p><p>But let's not be too haughty regarding our neighbor, the Mississippi of the Midwest, imparting certain ambitious knots of tissue with constitutional rights denied their surrounding flesh vessels. A law was introduced in the Illinois Senate earlier this year doing just that.</p><p>State Sen. Neil Anderson (R-Andalusia) proposed <a class="Link" href="https://capitolnewsillinois.com/news/illinois-republican-senator-pushes-to-outlaw-abortion-loses-leadership-spots/" target="_blank" >a fetal personhood bill</a> that would give a fertilized egg constitutional rights on Day One. Even abortion opponents cringed away from it — it raised the possibility of women having abortions being charged with first degree murder, though Anderson was quick to point out that wasn't his intent. "There’s nobody up here that wants to put women in jail," he said.</p><p>Why not? Because if the egg is a person, then wouldn't its destruction be murder and the individual doing so liable? Except of course if that individual is a woman and, the unstated logic goes, not a full human being, not completely in charge of her own destiny, which what the law says in the 13 states that bar abortion. A dynamic which, in essence, weighs the rights of the actual human woman and the fertilized egg and decides the egg is calling the shots, as God intended. (I hope the legislature never declares the pancreas to be a person, too, because I've been thwarting God's intentions for mine through medical science for nearly two years now.)</p><p>This is a complicated subject to dispatch in 795 words, so I want to leave you with a statistic that might not be generally known.</p><p>Roe v. Wade was reversed — the holy grail of the anti-abortion crowd — four years ago, and abortion in the United States has steadily gone up since then, from about 80,000 a month to around 100,000, thanks to a jump in abortions via mail — in pill form — and states such as Illinois throwing open their doors to surrounding red states. The aforementioned Abbey Hall came here to do what God intended to happen at some later time.</p><p>A reminder. Abortion is never going away because women — human beings, remember, at least in my book, with the capacity to determine their own morality and run their own lives — want it. What is in question is how difficult and expensive it will be to get.</p>

entries.title: White Sox fall flat in Minnesota finale, but take care of business in division entering home stretch
entries.summary: <p>MINNEAPOLIS — White Sox bats went silent Sunday to fall short of a sweep in Minnesota, losing 5-1 in the finale of a series that still saw them bury the Twins in the American League Central standings with a month to go in the regular season.</p><p>Twins starter Zebby Matthews took a perfect game into the sixth inning until No. 9 Sox hitter Drew Romo (.140/.229/.292) pulled a single to right field. </p><p>Matthews scattered four other hits over 8 1/3 innings with five strikeouts. Braden Montgomery got the Sox on the board in the ninth with an RBI single. </p><p>Minnesota hitters took full advantage of a bullpen day for the Sox, tagging opener Jordan Hicks for three runs, Tyler Gilbert for another and adding one more off bulk thrower <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox/2026/08/23/white-sox-jose-urquidy-shane-smith-kyle-teel-sam-antonacci-walker-mckinven-will-venable-carlos-quentin-franchise-record-hit-by-pitches-houston-astros" >Jose Urquidy</a>. He went five innings for a pitching staff <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox/2026/08/29/grant-taylor-white-sox-pitching-division-race" >desperate for coverage</a> with the calendar flipping to September.</p><p>By taking two out of three, the Sox put another game between themselves and the second-place Guardians while leaving Minnesota seven-and-a-half back with a month to go. The Twins put perennial Sox killer Byron Buxton back on the injured list Sunday with a hip injury.</p><p>The Sox head to Houston for another key series with the AL West-leading Astros.</p><div entries.title: White Sox hungry for Colson Montgomery, Munetaka Murakami to get cooking at the plate in final month
entries.summary: <p>MINNEAPOLIS — The American League’s highest-scoring offense has been doing it lately without much help from two of their biggest sluggers.</p><p>The <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox" target="_blank" ><u>White Sox</u></a> got a three-run bomb from shortstop Colson Montgomery in their series opener against the Twins, but he was still clawing his way out of <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox/2026/08/25/white-sox-shortstop-colson-montgomery-offensive-struggles-jake-burger-will-venable-derek-shomon-jacob-degrom-all-star-home-runs" target="_blank" ><u>a monthlong funk</u></a> entering play Sunday, with a .197/.264/.325 line over his past 30 games, including 53 strikeouts in 117 at-bats.</p><p>Rookie first baseman Munetaka Murakami hasn’t fared much better, slashing .156/.302/.365 in August with 44 strikeouts and going 10 games without a home run.</p><p>“With Mune, we can't forget all the new that goes into it,” Sox hitting director Ryan Fuller said. “His first year. It's August, we're closing in on September. There's a lot that goes into it and we know the preparation with Mune is always there — always good at-bats, and the work that he's putting in in the cage is great. So it's only a matter of time before he gets back to doing what he's going to do.”</p><p>Fuller’s been down this road before with Montgomery, following last year’s mid-season sabbatical in the desert to help the tall infielder rediscover his stroke.</p><p>“A lot of guys have ebbs and flows in that sophomore year, and he's doing a good job of maintaining and understanding what he needs to do to be successful,” Fuller said. “Looking forward to having him be a contributing factor down the stretch because we know he can be a game changer.”</p><p>Montgomery felt he was turning a corner in Minneapolis, too.</p><p>“The past couple games, my decision making and my process and approach at the plate has been a little more consistent,” he said. “I should be driving in more runs, or just a little better situational hitting. But I don't know, it's just baseball, you know?”</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" > <div class="TweetUrl"> <blockquote class="twitter-tweet"><p lang="en" dir="ltr">Colson Montgomery sent that one outta here! 🚀 <a href="https://t.co/h7gcDIT2Hb">pic.twitter.com/h7gcDIT2Hb</a></p>— Chicago White Sox (@whitesox) <a href="https://x.com/whitesox/status/2093495551333474607?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">August 29, 2026</a></blockquote> <script async src="https://platform.x.com/widgets.js" charset="utf-8"></script> </div> </div> </div></div><p>Between those sluggers’ streaks in the heart of the order has been third baseman Miguel Vargas’ <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox/2026/08/26/miguel-vargas-unbelievably-stable-skill-set-is-pacing-the-white-sox-offense-colson-montgomery-munetaka-murakami-will-venable-walker-mckinven-derek-shomon" target="_blank" ><u>remarkably consistent bat</u></a>, with a .979 OPS in August and a hitting approach that’s marking the organizational checkboxes of decisions, contact and damage.</p><p>“For Vargy in the past, it was great decisions, good contact, damage a little bit below average,” Fuller said. “This year, it's all three skills. One of the best decision-makers in MLB. Above-average contact rates, and now this year, with his body, his swing, improved bat speed — there's a lot of things we can point to.”</p><p>And picking up some historic slack lately has been Savannah Banana-turned-All-Star rookie <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox/2026/08/26/tristan-peters-white-sox-munetaka-murakami-colson-montgomery-franchise-record-frank-thomas-paul-konerko-carlos-lee-will-venable" >Tristan Peters</a>, who ended a second-half drought at the plate by raining home runs for five straight games, tying a franchise record. He’s carrying an absurd 1.235 OPS over his last 15 games.</p><p>“To see him have the stretch that he's on is incredible,” Fuller said. “But really more than anything, to learn those lessons and to be able to provide himself confidence when he does have a few bad days, of, 'I'll get it back,' is really encouraging.”</p><p>Just as incredible is the Sox’ position leading the AL with 651 runs scored, more than two dozen ahead of the next closest offense (Minnesota, 624), a year after scraping the bottom of the ranks in most offensive categories en route to a third straight triple-digit loss season.</p><p>Now firmly controlling their own destiny toward a division title, the Sox are second in their league in home runs (180) and OPS (.728).</p><p>“To go from 14th in runs per game in the AL to first — I mean, I’d be lying if I said that I thought it was going to be where we are right now,” Fuller said.</p><p>“Last year, the first year of the new hitting program, that was selling the vision of what could be. And now it's pointing to the players at the big-league level who are actually doing it,” he added. “So what it means to be a White Sox hitter now, we have tangible ways of showing them what we value. It's been a ton of fun… A lot to celebrate, and now looking to be able to do it into October.”</p>

entries.title: Trump to serve as chairman at western suburbs golf tournament in September
entries.summary: <p>President Donald Trump will return to the Chicago area next month to serve as the honorary chairman at the Presidents Cup golf tournament in the western suburbs.</p><p>PGA TOUR, the tournament's organizer, confirmed in a news release that Trump will attend the event happening Sept. 22-27 at the Medinah Country Club. The tournament includes 24 of the world’s top golfers — 12 from the U.S. versus 12 golfers from around the world, excluding Europe.</p><p>In a post on his social media platform Truth Social, Trump said he was honored to be selected as the chairman for the tournament. It will be his first public appearance in the Chicago area since his reelection.</p><p>“This will be a particularly exciting event. Both teams are 'loaded' with Talent. I look forward to being there, and greeting all of these fantastic athletes, on both teams!" he wrote. "See you in Chicago!"</p><p>It's the second time Trump has served as chairman at the tournament; he held the role during the 2017 Presidents Cup in New Jersey, according to PGA.</p><p>"The Presidents Cup has a proud tradition of engaging world leaders from across the globe and across political lines, and President Trump’s involvement continues that legacy," PGA TOUR CEO Brian Rolapp said in a statement. "His participation will help elevate the event on the international stage while furthering our mission of bringing people together through the game of golf.”</p><p>Past Presidents Joe Biden, Barack Obama and George Bush also served as the tournament's honorary chairmen, according to PGA.</p><p>Ahead of his reelection in 2024, Trump appeared publicly in Chicago twice. The National Association of Black Journalists <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/politics/2024/07/30/donald-trump-chicago-visit-national-association-of-black-journalists-backlash" target="_blank" >hosted him at the organization’s annual conference</a> in July 2024, a decision that drew internal and external backlash for NABJ. <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/elections/2024/10/15/president-trump-returns-chicago-tuesday-watch" target="_blank" >Trump appeared before a friendlier crowd</a> in October 2024 at The Economic Club of Chicago to discuss his plan to impose broad tariffs during his second term.</p>

entries.title: Hey, neighbor! Cubs begin pivotal stretch starting Monday with four-game series vs. Brewers
entries.summary: <p>Pessimistic Cubs fans can take solace in the fact that history shows their team still has a chance of seizing its first National League Central title since the COVID-shortened 60-game 2020 season.</p><p>It was only last season that the Guardians overcame an 11-game deficit with 23 games left to overtake the Tigers for the American League Central title.</p><p>And the 2018 Cubs held a five-game lead with 25 games left, only for the Brewers to win four of six games against them during a nine-game span to cut their lead to one before overtaking them for the division title.</p><p>The Cubs finished that season with a tiebreaker loss to the Brewers for the NL Central title and a wild-card defeat to the Rockies, prompting left-hander Jon Lester to suggest that perhaps they needed a certain part of their anatomy ‘‘knocked in the dirt to appreciate it. Maybe we needed that.’’</p><p>Unfortunately for the Cubs, the Brewers have shown no signs of complacency in their quest for their fourth consecutive division title and fifth NL Central crown in six seasons. They’re destined for their eighth playoff berth in the last nine seasons.</p><p>And manager Pat Murphy won’t let up, even with a comfortable lead as the Brewers open a four-game series Monday at Wrigley Field that starts a span of seven games in 10 days against the Cubs.</p><p>On Tuesday, Murphy pulled rookie shortstop Cooper Pratt after he failed to execute a bunt, then didn’t hustle on a shallow pop that fell safely but cost him a double.</p><p>Two days later, Pratt fouled a bunt attempt but finished the at-bat by hitting a sacrifice fly and received a hero’s welcome from his teammates, including several who had lectured him after his lapse Tuesday.</p><p>The Brewers have the best record in the majors, thanks in part to executing the details that have resulted in the largest run differential in the game, despite hitting the fewest home runs.</p><p>Murphy has pushed his players to their limits throughout the season, even scheduling infield practice before the second game of a three-game series at Arizona during a stretch of 18 games in 17 days before the All-Star break.</p><p>‘‘Being tired is for guys who pick another profession,’’ Murphy said after being asked by a reporter about not letting up on the pregame workload during a tedious stretch. ‘‘Professional bowling is not as taxing. I don’t know. But if you’re tired, get another job.</p><p>‘‘I’m tired, too. But they’re making me do it.’’</p><p>Murphy, 67, had surgery to repair a ruptured disk in late June but returned to the ballpark the next day. He has postponed surgery to replace his right hip until after the season, and the discomfort is noticeable when he makes lumbering visits to the mound and during postgame handshakes.</p><p>Meanwhile, the Brewers wisely have employed a six-man rotation for stretches to protect the arms of flame-throwing 14-game winner Jacob Misiorowski, who didn’t have a pitch clocked at 101 mph or faster for only the second time this season in a victory last week against the Mets, and Logan Henderson, who has allowed three runs or fewer in all of his first 19 career starts.</p><p>Misiorowski and Henderson are lined up to pitch the final two games of the four-game series against the Cubs.</p><p>Misiorowski still leads the majors with 1.73 ERA, and he has allowed three runs or fewer in each of his first 25 starts this season.</p><p>When the Brewers made their late push in 2018, the Cubs were in the midst of playing 35 games in 36 days, and fatigue struck the offense. They produced a slash line of .235/.300/.363. Willson Contreras had a .465 OPS in the final month and only three home runs after the All-Star break.</p><p>The Cubs had no attractive alternatives in the the second half for Ian Happ, who had hit 24 homers with a .842 OPS during an impressive 2017 rookie season. Happ had four homers with a .653 OPS after the All-Star break in 2018 and started the 2019 in the minors.</p><p>The Brewers also have the NL’s top bullpen with a 3.21 ERA entering Sunday. Left-hander Aaron Ashby is among the top five in appearances (63) and has averaged more than an inning per outing.</p><p>Abner Uribe hasn’t pitched since Aug. 9 because of a strained right flexor suffered after throwing 55 pitches in consecutive nights, and he is on a minor-league rehab stint.</p><p>Coincidentally, the Brewers finished their pre-All-Star break schedule by getting swept by the Pirates, only to return with four consecutive victories and 10 in their first 14 games after the break.</p><p>The Cubs were three games out of first place in the division on the morning of Aug. 15, but the Brewers responded with two victories at Dodger Stadium and have displayed impressive resiliency.</p><p>‘‘Control what you can control,’’ Cubs right-hander Colin Rea said before the Cubs lost two of three games to the Diamondbacks last week. ‘‘We can’t control what the Brewers do or the Padres or the Diamondbacks.’’</p><p>Failing to put a dent in the Brewers’ lead this week might accelerate the Cubs’ plans to focus on their reinforcements from the injured list. Availability and effectiveness will dictate the Cubs’ postseason roster.</p><p>Right-hander Ben Brown’s recurring neck discomfort takes away one late-inning strikeout weapon, and right-hander Edward Cabrera’s inconsistency and finger blister might relegate him to bullpen duty once he returns from the IL.</p><p>Shortstop Dansby Swanson’s return from an injured left oblique — which might happen after the Cubs and Brewers conclude their season series — merits scrutiny, although Nico Hoerner has held his own at shortstop and Matt Shaw’s return from a sprained hand improves the depth.</p><p>The Brewers also are navigating their share of ailments, most notably first baseman Jake Bauers’ shin splits. But Bauers, with 23 homers and 76 RBI, remains a strong candidate for comeback-player-of-the-year honors.</p><p>And even with a decent lead, Murphy won’t tolerate mental mishaps.</p><p>‘‘We’re on a journey,’’ Murphy, a two-time NL Manager of the Year, said after a game in which his players committed a couple of mental gaffes two months ago. ‘‘And we’re an inch from the top and we’re an inch from the bottom. And addressing those things is delicate.</p><p>‘‘There’s some growth there. There’s some understanding whenever you make [a mental error] like that, especially when it’s an aggressive thing. You don’t just hit everything head-on when you’ve got a 162-game season.</p><p>‘‘Sometimes you let it play out. You don’t let it go, you let it play out. Maybe somebody grabs it. Maybe there’s a better way to teach it.’’</p><p>At this point, Murphy’s methods have worked brilliantly.</p><p>‘‘Just keep floating down the road,’’ Murphy said of the big picture. ‘‘You can’t coast uphill. So we’ve got an uphill battle to what our standards are and what we want to accomplish. We’re going into it with that mentality.’’</p>

entries.title: Bears leave CB Kyler Gordon on PUP list to start season, ruling him out for first four games
entries.summary: <p>The <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a>’ drama with injured nickel cornerback <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/08/15/bears-coach-ben-johnson-expects-de-montez-sweat-lt-braxton-jones-soon-but-cb-kyler-gordon-still-unknown" target="_blank" >Kyler Gordon</a> will go on for at least another month. They left him on the physically unable-to-perform list at the roster deadline Sunday, meaning he’ll miss at least the first four games of the season.</p><p>They did the same with defensive lineman Shemar Turner (knee) and backup linebacker Noah Sewell (Achilles tendon). The earliest those three can play is Oct. 11 at the Packers.</p><p>Veteran safety/cornerback Cam Lewis or rookie cornerback Malik Muhammad likely will start in Gordon’s place. Muhammad has gotten most of the first-team reps lately.</p><p>The Bears likely will decide Monday whether to put offensive tackle Ozzy Trapilo (knee), running back Kyle Monangai (knee), tight end Hayden Large (unspecified) and defensive end Austin Booker (groin) on injured reserve. They needed to be on the 53-man roster at the deadline to be eligible to play this season.</p><p>Gordon was out all of training camp with a calf injury. The Bears have said little about his status, other than general manager Ryan Poles implying that Gordon hadn’t fully embraced the rehab program the team put together for him.</p><p>He missed 14 games last season with three injuries, leaving the Bears’ defense in a bind without one of its top players.</p>
